question: Using the Gmail connector, a user asks Claude to summarize the contents of a PDF attached to an email. What limitation should the user expect?
options: A) Claude can read the email metadata and body but cannot open the attachment's content.
B) Claude cannot access the email at all until the attachment is first removed.
C) Claude can read the attachment content, but only when it stays under 10MB in size.
D) Claude can read the attachment content, but only when the attachment is a PDF file type.
correct_answers: A) Claude can read the email metadata and body but cannot open the attachment's content.
explanations: Correct. The Gmail connector exposes metadata and body content but does not process attachment content, so the PDF's contents remain inaccessible.
Incorrect. Claude can still read the surrounding email even with an attachment present; only the attachment content is off-limits.
Incorrect. There is no documented size threshold that unlocks attachment reading; content stays inaccessible regardless of size.
Incorrect. Attachment content is inaccessible for any file type, not just non-PDF formats.
